To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have synthesized and studied a new halogen‐bond‐based rotaxane host that can selectively bind iodide over the other halide anions, in aqueous solution.

the halogen‐boning rotaxane is the first example of a rotaxane host that can selectively sense anions in aqueous solution and that the halogen bond is an effective supramolecular interaction for the design of anion sensors.
the first halogen bonding rotaxane host has been synthesized and its anion‐binding and luminescence properties investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new halogen‐bonded supramolecular assemblies and the development of their anion recognition and sensing properties in water.
halogen bonding in the context of supramolecular chemistry, with a particular focus on anion recognition and sensing in water.
the development of new supramolecular hosts that bind and sense anions in aqueous media, through the use of halogen‐bond donors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the halogen‐bonds are strong and directional, but not strong enough to compete with water in aqueous solution.
the halogen‐bonds of the halogen‐acceptor component in this rotaxane are sufficiently strong to allow selective anion binding and recognition, but not sufficiently strong to prevent anion exchange.
the rotaxane is an excellent anion receptor and a highly sensitive anion sensor in water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
halogen bonding is a useful tool to create new anion receptors in water.
we developed the first halogen bonding-based interlocked host to sense anion in water.
the halogen‐binding rotaxane is a selective anion‐sensor for iodide in water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
halogen‐bonded hosts are viable for anion recognition in water.
the halogen‐bonds can be used to design rotaxanes that are capable of anion recognition and sensing in water.
the halogen‐boning rotaxane is a highly effective anion‐recording sensor in water, and the first of its kind to do so.
